Containers.Name: Unwake
Containers.Description: Keeps the directory trees of your user shares in RAM, so folder listings, name lookups and attribute reads don't wake sleeping disks - not even after a backup or a big copy pushed everything else out of memory. Replaces Dynamix Cache Directories.
Containers.ExtraSearchTerms: cache directories folder caching spin up spindown wake disk smb browse
Containers.Overview:
Unwake runs a small FUSE daemon on top of /mnt/user (shfs stays underneath) and answers folder listings, name lookups, attributes and extended attributes from its own tree in RAM. It reads a disk's folders only while that disk spins anyway and follows every change via fanotify, so nothing is re-read on a timer and nothing pushes the tree out of memory.
Features: - Folders in RAM, for good: listings, lookups (including of names that don't exist), attributes and extended attributes without touching the disks - Never wakes a disk to fill the cache: folders are read while a disk spins anyway, at idle priority - Kept current via fanotify: Mover, Unspin, direct writes to /mnt/diskN, containers, ZFS datasets - File data through the kernel (FUSE passthrough), files on one known disk read from that disk directly - Shares in RAM: every share with a tick box, SSD-pool-only shares go straight to their pool - Verifier: the folders in RAM are checked against the disks while they spin, differences repaired and logged - Spin-up log: what Unwake passed to shfs before each disk spun up - Updates in place, without stopping the array or closing open files
